blurb:
If you've got someone in your house under 25, they already know who Yeat is. If you're the one buying the tickets, consider this your crash course: he's one of the most streamed artists in rap right now, known for a sound that's dense, layered, and loud in the best possible way.

He hits the Coca-Cola Roxy on Tuesday, September 22nd. The Roxy is an ideal room for this kind of show, big enough to feel like an event, intimate enough to actually feel the bass. If you've been looking for a reason to introduce someone younger to a real concert experience, or if you already know every word, either way this one delivers.

Get tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Yeat skews younger than the median Perimeter Post reader at 38, but the audience has a young professional segment and likely parents of teens/young adults. The Roxy is a familiar, accessible venue. Lower demographic fit than Chelsea Handler or Suki Waterhouse, but still a legitimate one-night concert worth surfacing.

event_name: To The Limit: The Ultimate Eagles Experience
blurb:
The Eagles catalog is one of those things that sounds like it belongs in an elevator until you're actually hearing 'Hotel California' or 'Desperado' live in a real room, and then it hits completely differently. To The Limit is a nationally touring Eagles tribute act with a reputation for doing this right, not a local bar cover band doing their best, but a group that's played prestigious theaters around the country and has built a real following doing exactly this.

They're at The Strand Theatre in Marietta on Friday, October 2nd. The Strand is a beautiful historic venue on the Square, and it's the right size for a show like this: close enough to feel it, big enough to be a proper event. VIP tickets are available and include early access, a pre-show mini-concert, meet and greet, two drink tickets, and a signed poster. The VIP window opens at 6:30pm, lobby for regular admission at 7pm, showtime at 8.

For empty nesters or anyone who grew up with these songs in heavy rotation, this is a great Friday night.
scoring_notes: The Eagles demographic skews toward the 45-65 empty nester portion of the Perimeter Post audience. The Strand is a well-loved local venue with strong goodwill. Tribute acts are not rare, but To The Limit has a national touring profile which lifts the uniqueness score. VIP package adds a premium tier that fits the $105K HHI audience well.

event_name: Tapestry Tunes: A Carole King Tribute Cabaret
blurb:
The Tapestry album came out in 1971. It sat at number one for six straight years. If you grew up hearing 'You've Got a Friend' or 'I Feel the Earth Move,' you didn't just hear those songs, you felt them. They're the kind of thing that sticks.

On Sunday, September 27th, The Alley Stage on the Marietta Square is hosting Tapestry Tunes, a Carole King tribute cabaret featuring Bethany Irby, who recently played the lead in Aurora Theatre's 'Beautiful: The Carole King Musical.' This isn't a cover band at a bar. Irby is the real deal, a trained vocalist with 20 years of Atlanta stage credits, and the cabaret format means it's an intimate, close-up experience that a big theatre production can't replicate.

This one is great for empty nesters or anyone looking for a genuinely warm night out that doesn't require earplugs. Grab tickets soon, a show like this in a small room fills up fast.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the empty nester segment of the Perimeter Post audience. Carole King's catalog has broad generational appeal across 40-65 year olds. Cabaret format in a small venue adds intimacy and uniqueness. Slightly lower demographic fit for younger readers, but the mixed audience skew means this serves a real slice of the readership.

event_name: Guided Tasting & Tour at ASW Distillery
blurb:
ASW Distillery sits right in the Battery area and makes some genuinely award-winning craft gin and vodka. On Sunday, September 27th, they're running a guided tasting and tour: four pours led by one of their experienced guides, followed by a behind-the-scenes look at how the spirits are distilled on their copper hybrid still.

The whole thing runs about 90 minutes and starts at 2pm, which makes it a natural anchor for an afternoon. Grab brunch beforehand, do the tour, and you've got a complete Sunday without driving all over town. For couples or small groups who want something a little more interesting than a restaurant, this is a solid call.

They ask you to arrive 15 minutes early for parking and check-in. You can grab a drink while you wait, which is a very reasonable policy.
scoring_notes: Distillery tours run regularly, so uniqueness is moderate, but the demographic fit is strong for the Perimeter Post's educated, $105K HHI, adult-leaning readership. ASW is a well-regarded local brand and the Battery location is familiar territory for this audience. Good pairing activity for couples and small groups. Weekday casual tone works for Sunday afternoon framing.

venue: The Block at You42 Studios, Metro Atlanta
blurb:
BONNIE X CLYDE are bringing their festival sound to The Block at You42 Studios for a one-night-only 360° Boiler Room-style show on Friday, September 25th. The format alone is worth paying attention to: instead of a traditional stage setup, the crowd surrounds the performance from all sides, which turns a concert into something closer to a real shared experience.

BONNIE X CLYDE have been a fixture at major electronic music festivals for years, known for a high-energy, genre-blending set that doesn't really have an off switch. If you've been to one of those festivals and thought 'I wish I could just see them in a smaller room,' this is that night.

Doors at 9pm, runs to 2am. This is a late-night pick, not a dinner-and-home situation. But for the right crowd, it's the kind of Friday that makes the rest of the weekend feel earned.
scoring_notes: The 360° Boiler Room format is genuinely unique and differentiates this from a standard club night. Skews toward the younger professional segment of the Perimeter Post audience. Late-night start (9pm to 2am) limits appeal for families and older empty nesters, but for young professionals this is a standout pick. Uniqueness score is high because the format itself is rare locally.

blurb:
Suki Waterhouse has been quietly building one of the more interesting careers in indie pop. She started releasing music in 2016, spent years developing a dreamy, understated sound, and then her song 'Good Looking' blew up in a way that felt genuinely earned rather than manufactured. Now she's on a real tour, and she's stopping at the Coca-Cola Roxy on Tuesday, September 29th.

This is the kind of show that sells out and then people are annoyed they missed it. The Roxy is a great room for her vibe, not too big, good sound, and the Battery area gives you plenty of dinner options before the show if you want to make a full night of it.

Tickets are available now. Don't wait on this one.
scoring_notes: Waterhouse fits well with the 38 median age, educated, adult-leaning Perimeter Post reader. She has crossover appeal between younger millennials and older Gen Z. One-night concert at a premium venue, and her recent surge in popularity makes this feel timely and relevant. Strong pick for young professionals and couples looking for a night out.

venue: Mimms Museum of Technology and Art, Roswell
blurb:
Randy Wigginton helped write the software for the Apple II and the original Macintosh. After that he went on to shape things at eBay, Google, Square, and Block. He's been at the center of basically every major wave in modern computing, and on Saturday, September 19th, he's going to sit down at the Mimms Museum of Technology and Art in Roswell and just... tell you about it.

For a room full of people who work in tech, manage teams that run on tech, or are raising kids who will eventually inherit all of this, that's a pretty compelling two hours. These are not TED Talk-style highlights either. This is a guy with five decades of firsthand stories, including the people, the breakthroughs, and the moments that didn't go according to plan.

The Mimms Museum is a gem of a venue that a lot of locals haven't been to yet. This is a good reason to fix that. Details and tickets are on their site.
scoring_notes: Perimeter Post skews toward highly educated ($105K HHI, 70% bachelor's+), tech-adjacent professionals. Randy Wigginton's resume (Apple II, Mac, Google, eBay) is DIRECTLY relevant to this audience. One-time speaking event at a niche museum venue adds uniqueness. High intellectual interest match. Strong pick.

blurb:
Chelsea Handler does not do polite. She does honest, unfiltered, and genuinely funny in a way that makes you laugh out loud and then feel slightly guilty about it. And she's bringing that exact energy to the Coca-Cola Roxy on Friday, October 2nd.

This is a real stand-up night out, not a panel or a podcast taping or some watered-down speaking event. Handler has been doing this for 20+ years and she gets sharper with age. If you've got a group of friends who are overdue for a proper evening that doesn't involve a kid's soccer schedule or a work happy hour, this is your excuse.

Tickets are moving. Grab yours now before you're stuck watching the highlights on someone else's Instagram story.
scoring_notes: Chelsea Handler skews perfectly toward the Perimeter Post audience: educated, adult-leaning, $105K household income, 38 median age. Stand-up comedy at a premium venue is a natural fit. High adult skew, one-night-only event, and the Roxy is a well-known destination venue. Strong pick for the mix of young professionals and empty nesters in this readership.

blurb: Chelsea Handler is one of those performers where you already know if you're in or out, and if you're in, you don't need a lot of convincing. She's been one of the sharpest, most unapologetically honest voices in comedy for years, and the Coca-Cola Roxy at The Battery is a legitimately great venue to see her. Good sightlines, great energy, and you can make a full night of it with dinner before the show — The Battery has no shortage of options. Show starts at 8pm on Friday, October 2nd. If you've been meaning to get out of East Cobb for a real night out, this is a clean excuse with a hard deadline.
scoring_notes: Chelsea Handler skews toward the 35-55 educated female audience, which is well-represented in East Cobb. The Roxy at The Battery is a slightly longer drive but a premium experience that fits the income level. October 2 is just outside the core 'this week' window but still relevant for a newsletter sending mid-September. The Battery's dining and entertainment complex adds value to the outing.

event_name: Gary Owen: No Hard Feelings Tour
venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta, GA
blurb: Gary Owen has been making people lose it in comedy clubs for over 20 years, and he's getting sharper with age. The No Hard Feelings Tour stops at Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre for a night of the kind of comedy that's actually funny — bold, personal, a little rough around the edges, and completely unapologetic about it. He draws from his military background, his family life, and the kind of everyday moments that hit different when someone puts the right words to them. Fair warning: this show is recommended for 18 and up, so leave the teenagers at home and make it a proper adults-only night out. If you and your partner haven't had a real date night lately, here's your excuse.
scoring_notes: Good adult-skewing event for East Cobb's 42-median-age audience. Cobb Energy is convenient and well-regarded. Gary Owen's military background and relatable family humor plays well for suburban audiences. The 18+ note actually works in its favor for East Cobb's empty nester segment — gives them a reason to treat it as a real night out. Touring show with a specific date gives it urgency.

blurb: Oktoberfest season is here and Glover Park Brewery is doing it right. Three days of celebrating right on Marietta Square — good beer, good people, and exactly the kind of fall vibe you've been waiting for since Labor Day ended. Glover Park is already one of the better spots in the area, and when they lean into a theme like this, it tends to be worth showing up for. Whether you're going on Thursday to beat the weekend crowd or rolling through on Saturday with a group, it's an easy yes. Fall doesn't feel like fall in East Cobb until you've had a cold lager outside with decent company. This is your moment.
scoring_notes: Solid adult-skewing event that fits East Cobb's $118K median income crowd well. Three-day run means flexible attendance. Marietta Square location is highly convenient for East Cobb residents. Not a weekly recurring thing — Oktoberfest is a once-a-year event with genuine seasonal energy. Good fit for the empty nester and established family segments who enjoy local brewery culture.

event_name: True Crimes Seminar: The Atlanta Child Murders
venue: North Cobb Senior Center, Acworth, GA
blurb: If you've ever gone down a true crime rabbit hole and found yourself reading about the Atlanta Child Murders case at midnight, this one is for you. Switzer Library is hosting a True Crimes Seminar that digs into the 1979 to 1981 murders and how microscopic fiber analysis and mathematical probability ultimately led to the conviction of Wayne Williams. That forensic breakthrough set a massive legal precedent that still matters today. The seminar also covers recent DNA retesting on the case, which means there's genuinely new ground to cover — this isn't just a retelling of something you already know. It's one hour, no ticket required, and the kind of afternoon that'll have you talking about it for days.
scoring_notes: Highly unique event — not a recurring series, not a generic community talk. The Atlanta Child Murders case is deeply locally relevant and culturally significant, which plays well for an educated East Cobb audience. Free and accessible. Strong conversation-starter for the 40s-and-up crowd. The modern DNA update angle pushes it from history lesson to genuinely current.

blurb: Sixty years. That's how long the Roswell Arts Festival has been bringing the community out to celebrate local artists, live music, and good food. This isn't some small pop-up market — it's a full two-day event with more than 80 artists on display, live entertainment, kids' activities, and a solid lineup of food trucks to keep everyone fueled up. Every dollar raised goes back into Roswell Parks and Recreation programs, so you're supporting something real when you show up. The 60th anniversary makes this one feel a little more special than your average fall festival. Bring the family, walk the grounds, and grab something you'll actually hang on your wall.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for East Cobb's established family and empty nester mix. The 60th anniversary adds a can't-miss quality that a typical annual festival doesn't have. Free admission is a bonus but not the selling point — the community legacy angle is. Kicks off the upcoming weekend (Sept 19), so timing is perfect for the newsletter send.

event_name: To The Limit: The Ultimate Eagles Experience
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta, GA
blurb: The Strand Theatre on Marietta Square doesn't do mediocre shows — and To The Limit: The Ultimate Eagles Experience is not a mediocre tribute band. These guys have built their reputation performing at theaters and festivals across the country by doing one thing obsessively well: recreating what an Eagles concert actually felt like. The harmonies on 'Hotel California,' the guitar work on 'Life in the Fast Lane,' the full emotional arc of a night when rock and roll was at its peak. VIP tickets are available if you want to go all-in — early access seating, a pre-show mini-concert, meet and greet with the band, two drink tickets, and a signed poster. Main show starts at 8pm. The Strand is one of the best rooms in the area to hear live music. If you grew up with The Eagles, this is worth the drive from East Cobb, and it's barely a drive at all.
scoring_notes: Eagles catalog skews perfectly toward East Cobb's 42-median-age and older crowd. The Strand Theatre is a premium intimate venue that justifies the ticket price at a $118K median income level. VIP option adds an aspirational tier that plays well for this audience. Marietta Square location is a strong geographic pull for East Cobb residents. The specific October 2 date and venue make it a real event with urgency.

venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta, GA
blurb: The Indigo Girls grew up playing clubs around Atlanta before they went on to sell millions of records worldwide. Coming back to perform at Cobb Energy feels like a homecoming in the best possible way. Emily Saliers and Amy Ray have been making music together for four decades — the kind of harmonies and songwriting that hold up because they were built on something real. If 'Closer to Fine' or 'Kid Fears' has ever been the song playing in the background of a meaningful moment in your life, you already know whether you're going. Grammy-winning producer Linda Perry is also part of the night, which adds another layer to what's already a stacked lineup. Cobb Energy is right in your neighborhood. This one doesn't need much convincing.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for East Cobb's educated, 42-median-age audience with the disposable income to buy real concert tickets. The Atlanta roots angle makes it locally resonant. Indigo Girls have a multigenerational fanbase that spans the established family and empty nester segments East Cobb skews toward. Cobb Energy is a premium venue experience that matches the income level. Not a recurring event.

event_name: Tapestry Tunes: A Carole King Tribute Cabaret
blurb: If Carole King's Tapestry album was on rotation in your house growing up, this is your night out. The Alley Stage on Marietta Square is hosting Tapestry Tunes, a cabaret-style tribute to one of the most iconic albums in American music history — and the performer, Bethany Irby, isn't some random tribute act. She just finished playing the lead role in 'Beautiful: The Carole King Musical' at Aurora Theatre, so she knows this material cold. You're getting 'You've Got a Friend,' 'I Feel the Earth Move,' 'So Far Away' — the full catalog, performed by someone who's genuinely built a career around it. Intimate venue, killer setlist, and an evening that feels like more than just dinner and a show. East Cobb's Marietta Square is basically right in your backyard. Make the drive.
scoring_notes: Near-perfect demographic fit. East Cobb's median age of 42, skewing toward empty nesters and established families, means Carole King's catalog hits directly in the sweet spot of lived musical memory. The Alley Stage is an intimate, upscale-casual venue that matches the income level. Bethany Irby's Aurora Theatre credentials add real artistic legitimacy. Unique, not recurring.

blurb:
This one is genuinely different from your standard night out. The William Root House is an 1840s home surrounded by gardens that most people drive past without ever stepping inside, and this dinner is your reason to finally go.

You'll sit at antique farmhouse tables in the garden, work through a southern-style spread of fried chicken, seasonal vegetables, appetizers, and dessert, and actually feel like you're somewhere. Not a restaurant. Not a banquet hall. Somewhere that has a little history and a lot of atmosphere.

Space is limited, which means it's not going to be crowded and chaotic. It's the opposite of that. Bring your own drinks, bring someone worth spending an evening with, and go enjoy something that Marietta doesn't offer every weekend.
scoring_notes: High-income, educated East Cobb audience skews toward experiential dining and local history. The limited-seating garden dinner format at a historic home is genuinely rare, not a weekly recurring event. Strong match for both couples and established families looking for something with personality. Adult-leaning but not age-exclusive.
